The development-only C# recipe in ../reference/dictionary-interface.cs executes genuine Windows .NET Framework IDictionary<string,int>, Dictionary<string,int> and a separate tracing user implementation. Regenerate with Windows PowerShell and ../reference/generate-dictionary-interface.ps1. Neither the original Pascal compiler nor the native interpreter generates expected outcomes. Managed tools and runtimes are not installed with the application.

The 1200 outcomes cover 21 operations on native and user dictionaries: both inherited Add/Remove overloads, Count, IsReadOnly, Clear, Contains, CopyTo, enumeration, live read-only Keys/Values, indexed reads/writes, ContainsKey, TryGetValue, ICollection and IEnumerable upcasts, Enumerable Count/ToArray and compound indexed writes. Inputs include empty/populated dictionaries, nil receivers, present/missing/nil keys, matching/mismatching values and valid/invalid copy offsets. Traces record callbacks and output before errors. ArgumentNull/NullReference map to E_NIL, missing keys to E_KEY_NOT_FOUND, duplicate keys to E_KEY_DUPLICATE, copy bounds to E_RANGE and unsupported view mutations to E_READONLY.

The strongly typed Pascal fixture is compiled once and executed freshly per row. Columns are implementation, operation, initial size, nil receiver flag, key choice, value, copy offset, UTF-16 hexadecimal stdout (- means empty), and error code. JSON hashes normalize CRLF to LF. The test also checks bilingual diagnostics, static rejection before output, record copies, checked interface casts and forged metadata rejection.

The native closed contract has sixteen slots: the eight ICollection<KeyValuePair<K,V>> slots, Keys and Values returning ICollection<K>/ICollection<V>, default Item getter/setter, ContainsKey(K), Add(K,V), Remove(K), and TryGetValue(K,var V). It inherits IEnumerable through ICollection. Native dispatch reuses Dictionary storage and its comparer; user dispatch selects verified typed class methods. There is no runtime method-name or generic-type inference.

Required language support includes overloaded class and user-interface methods, inherited overload sets, matching external definitions and property accessors by signature, and call selection using known argument types. Selected tests exercise numeric specificity, var arguments, default parameters, params arrays, lambdas, duplicate signatures and ambiguity. These checks do not establish all Pascal overload-resolution rules. Global routine/constructor overloads, general source generics, record interface implementations, class inheritance, source-unit loading and the remainder of the library remain unfinished.
